## Motivation

Provide an Ornith-1.5 deployment guide alongside the existing Ornith-1.0 cookbook.

## Modifications

Add an Ornith-1.5 cookbook page with interactive deployment commands for 9B, 35B-A3B, 122B, and 397B, plus the published 35B-A3B and 397B FP8 checkpoints. Recipes cover H100 and H200 where configured, including 8-GPU TP=8 deployment for 122B on both platforms. All examples use the `ornith-ai` model repositories, port 30000, and the `qwen3` / `qwen3_coder` parsers.

Document model architecture, sampling settings, OpenAI-compatible chat and tool calling, and agent integration using the official model cards and 122B configuration. Add the navigation entry, point the DeepReinforce overview card to 1.5, and retain the 1.0 page.

Includes a separate one-line fix removing an extra closing brace in `docs/src/snippets/configs/popular-models.jsx`, which otherwise prevents the documentation from parsing.

## Accuracy Tests

Documentation-only change; model forward code is unchanged. GPU inference and accuracy were not measured, so recipes retain the unverified status.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable; no serving-performance changes or benchmark results are claimed.

## Documentation Validation

- Mintlify strict full-site prebuild validation passed.
- `mint broken-links` passed.
- Chrome checks passed for all 11 deployment combinations in both Python and Docker modes, including model paths, port mapping, reasoning/tool parsers, cURL payload synchronization, and absence of browser JavaScript errors.
- MDX/JSX parsing, generated cURL JSON, Python example syntax, and `git diff --check` passed.

@@ -1,7 +1,6 @@
 ---
 title: Ornith-1.0
 description: "Deploy DeepReinforce Ornith-1.0 with SGLang - a self-improving agentic-coding model family with 397B, 35B, and 9B checkpoints plus FP8 and GGUF variants."
-tag: NEW
 ---
 
 ## Deployment

@@ -0,0 +1,172 @@ +--- +title: Ornith-1.5 +description: "Deploy Ornith-1.5 with SGLang on NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs, with recipes for 9B, 35B-A3B, 122B, and 397B models, FP8, reasoning, and tool calling." +tag: NEW +--- + +import { Deployment } from "/src/snippets/_deployment.jsx"; +import { config } from "/src/snippets/configs/ornith-ai/ornith-1.5.jsx"; + +## Deployment + +These recipes target a single Linux node with NVIDIA CUDA GPUs. The Ornith-1.5 model cards recommend SGLang `>=0.5.9`. Both parsers are included in every launch command: `qwen3` separates reasoning from the answer, and `qwen3_coder` parses tool calls. + + + + + + +```bash Command +pip install --upgrade "sglang>=0.5.9" +``` + +Run the Python command from the deployment panel in this environment. See the [installation guide](/docs/get-started/install) for platform-specific requirements. + + + + +```bash Command +docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:latest +``` + +Select Docker in the deployment panel to generate the container command. + + + + + + +Choose your hardware, model size, and checkpoint format. The 9B recipe uses one GPU, 35B-A3B uses two, and 122B and 397B use eight. BF16 397B requires H200 in this matrix; its FP8 checkpoint is also available on H100. Select **BF16** for a BF16 checkpoint or **FP8** for an FP8 checkpoint. All commands use Hugging Face repository IDs and default to port **30000**. + + + +## 1. Model introduction + +Ornith-1.5 is an agentic model family published by [Ornith AI](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai). The 9B, 35B-A3B, 122B, and 397B checkpoints use Qwen3.5 architectures. The family extends Ornith-1.0's self-improvement loop by jointly optimizing task generation, scaffold construction, and solution rollouts through reinforcement learning. The model cards describe applications in coding, reasoning, and tool-using agents. + +The recipes expose an OpenAI-compatible API with separate reasoning output, parsed tool calls, and a 262,144-token context window. The table lists the checkpoints covered by this recipe. + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + + +
CheckpointFormatRecipe
Ornith-1.5-9BBF16Dense; 1× H100 or H200
Ornith-1.5-35B-A3BBF16MoE, ~3B active; 2× H100 or H200
Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B-FP8FP82× H100 or H200
Ornith-1.5-122BBF16MoE, 256 experts with 8 routed per token; 8× H100 or H200
Ornith-1.5-397BBF16MoE; 8× H200
Ornith-1.5-397B-FP8FP88× H100 or H200
+ +The official [9B](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-9B), [35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B), [122B](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-122B), and [397B](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/Ornith-1.5-397B) model cards declare the MIT license. + +**Resources:** [Ornith-1.5 model repositories](https://huggingface.co/ornith-ai/models?search=Ornith-1.5) · [Ornith-1.5 blog](https://ornith.ai/ornith_1_5.html) + +## 2. Configuration tips + +- **Model IDs:** use the `ornith-ai` namespace. The 35B repository includes the `-A3B` suffix. FP8 selections use the actual `-FP8` repository rather than the BF16 repository shown in their model-card quickstarts. +- **Context and memory:** every recipe uses `--context-length 262144`. The 9B, 35B-A3B, and 397B recipes use `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`; the 122B recipe uses `0.80`. Lower the context length if you need more memory headroom. +- **Reasoning:** `--reasoning-parser qwen3` exposes reasoning as `message.reasoning_content`, with the answer in `message.content`. +- **Tool calling:** `--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder` exposes parsed calls in `message.tool_calls`. Your application executes the requested function and submits its result in a follow-up tool message. +- **Sampling:** 35B-A3B and 397B recommend `temperature=0.6`, `top_p=0.95`, and `top_k=20`. For 9B and 122B, the model cards recommend `temperature=1.0` and `presence_penalty=1.5` for general tasks, or `temperature=0.6` and `presence_penalty=0.0` for precise coding; both use `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0.0`, and `repetition_penalty=1.0`. These settings are distinct from benchmark-specific settings. The Python examples below use the precise-coding sampling settings. + +## 3. Usage examples + +These requests use the precise-coding sampling settings shared by 9B and 122B. Set `model` to the deployment panel's `--served-model-name`, such as `Ornith-1.5-9B` or `Ornith-1.5-122B`. The examples use the default port; match the client port if you change the launch port. + + + +```python Example +from openai import OpenAI + +client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ornith-1.5-9B", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a compact Python is_prime function."}], + temperature=0.6, + top_p=0.95, + presence_penalty=0.0, + max_tokens=1024, + extra_body={"top_k": 20, "min_p": 0.0, "repetition_penalty": 1.0}, +) +message = response.choices[0].message +print("Reasoning:", getattr(message, "reasoning_content", None)) +print("Answer:", message.content) +``` + + + + + +```python Example +from openai import OpenAI + +client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:30000/v1", api_key="EMPTY") +response = client.chat.completions.create( + model="Ornith-1.5-9B", + messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Run the parser module's unit tests."}], + tools=[{ + "type": "function", + "function": { + "name": "run_tests", + "description": "Run the project's test suite.", + "parameters": { + "type": "object", + "properties": {"target": {"type": "string"}}, + "required": ["target"], + }, + }, + }], + tool_choice="auto", + temperature=0.6, + top_p=0.95, + presence_penalty=0.0, + max_tokens=2048, + extra_body={"top_k": 20, "min_p": 0.0, "repetition_penalty": 1.0}, +) +message = response.choices[0].message +print("Reasoning:", getattr(message, "reasoning_content", None)) +print("Tool calls:", message.tool_calls) +``` + + + +### Agent integration + +Configure your agent or coding CLI to use the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint: + +- **API base URL:** `http://localhost:30000/v1`. +- **API key:** `EMPTY` for a local server without API-key authentication. +- **Model:** the selected checkpoint's `--served-model-name`, such as `Ornith-1.5-122B`. + +Use the served model name rather than the Hugging Face repository ID when the two differ. Keep both parsers enabled so the agent receives separate reasoning and structured tool calls. Your agent executes tools and returns their results to the server in subsequent messages.
